alignments.note: Anarthrous noun with supplied determiner as a rule 7 helper (rule 51's anarthrous clause), headed on the noun.

δέ → even. The ASV writes *even* unitalicized at exactly the particle's position, and rule 11 makes that markup evidence: an unitalicized word answers to a source token. The explicative δέ is what it answers to, so rule 70's English-side test aligns the particle to the word the ASV wrote for it rather than leaving it empty. Rule 105's noun arm is the competing reading — folding *even* onto δικαιοσύνη as a supplied appositional helper — and it is refused here because that rule speaks of a *supplied* word and no unspent conjunction stands in its examples (COL.2.2, EPH.4.15).
The objective genitive takes the English case preposition under rule 21, headed on the name; the ASV's margin records *of*.
The second name is separately recoverable and stands as its own unit (rule 26).
εἰς → unto. SBLGNT.ROM.3.22.v008 selects r00-base, so the ASV's noted longer reading *and upon all* is not in the projection.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32).
The participle keeps the relativizer and its own verb (rule 32).
οὐ → no; no quantifier stands here, so rule 87 is not in question.
Existential *there is*, the expletive subject riding as a helper.

review_notes: Corrected: *even* moved from δικαιοσύνη's unit to δέ, which the accepted alignment left `unrepresented`. The evidence marks the ASV's supplied words with asterisks (as at 3:25 *to* *be* and 3:26 *I* *say*), and t001 carries none, so *even* is not italicized and answers to a source token; the explicative δέ standing in that slot is the only candidate, and rule 70's English-side test aligns a particle to whatever word the ASV wrote for it.
δικαιοσύνη keeps *the righteousness*, the supplied determiner riding as a rule 7 helper under rule 51's anarthrous clause.
Rule 105's noun-carrier fold remains the competing reading and is named in the δέ unit's note; that rule's own precedent is two units and its examples carry no unspent conjunction.
